clue.text: A penny to see doctor — that's cool

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny in British money
lo is an old word meaning look or see, as in lo and behold
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Someone takes a penny to the doctor and calls that a cool move.
explanation.definitionFit: Composure and self-assurance under pressure is what being cool means, a synonym for poise.

clue.text: Mexican inhabitant orders unopened ballot box

indicators.note: orders as a verb means arranges, so the remaining letters are put into a new arrangement
unopened says each word loses its opening letter, the B at the front of both

explanation.surface: A Mexican resident sends off for a ballot box that arrives still sealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' strips the first letter of each word, leaving ALLOT and OX; 'orders' then rearranges ALLOTOX.
explanation.definitionFit: The axolotl is a salamander native to lakes near Mexico City, so it is literally a Mexican inhabitant.

clue.text: 8 happy to get secular rights included

indicators.note: included says one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: lay means not belonging to the clergy, secular
R is the abbreviation for right, so two of them are RR

explanation.surface: Someone is cheerfully pleased to win secular rights in some charter.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is IDIOMATICALLY: the clues that cite it complete a common simile, here 'as happy as ___'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'as happy as Larry' means extremely content; the name completes that stock phrase.

clue.text: 8 keen celebrity mired?

indicators.note: the question mark flags that mired must also be read as being in the mud, so the star goes inside

parts.note: to be mired is to be stuck in mud, so the word gives the mud itself
a celebrity is a star

explanation.surface: An eager famous person ends up stuck in a bog.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is IDIOMATICALLY: the clues citing it complete a stock simile, here 'as keen as ___'. The question mark turns 'mired' into a mud-and-inside instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock simile 'as keen as mustard' means very enthusiastic, so the condiment completes it.

clue.text: 8 sick repeat

definitions.meaning: with 8 read as idiomatically, 'as sick as a ___' completes the British phrase for bitterly disappointed
to repeat words mindlessly is to echo them like a talking bird

explanation.surface: Someone ill keeps saying the same thing over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sick as a parrot' is British slang, much used by footballers, for being gutted by a result.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird completes the simile 'sick as a parrot', and as a verb it means mimic or echo words.

clue.text: Appeal from you or me, at last, after everybody

indicators.note: after places the letters from the last letters behind those for everybody

parts.note: everybody means all

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: An appeal is made by one of us, finally, after everyone else has spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Allure as a noun is attractiveness or charm, which is appeal in the sense of being attractive.

clue.text: Parts in current set-up or in ugly sisters

indicators.note: in puts the small word inside the rearranged letters
ugly suggests something misshapen, so these letters are put out of shape

explanation.surface: A pantomime's ugly sisters have a part to play in some arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ugly Sisters are Cinderella's stepsisters, stock villains of British pantomime; 'current' is electrical, not topical.
explanation.definitionFit: Resistors are components in an electrical circuit, parts placed in a set-up that carries current.

clue.text: Pain of love with jollies camping?

indicators.note: the question mark flags that camping must also be read as being in a tent, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: camping means staying under canvas, which gives a tent
love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O
jollies is old slang for Royal Marines, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: Love and good times on a camping holiday turn out painful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jollies' looks like fun times but is old naval slang for the Royal Marines. Love is O, the tennis zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is severe suffering, a synonym for great pain.

clue.text: How we can speak in a stupid way when mother's out

indicators.note: with mother out the answer becomes the other phrase, so her letters belong inside it

parts.note: in a stupid way means idiotically
mother is ma; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: We talk foolishly whenever mum isn't around.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: take MA out of the answer and you get 'in a stupid way'. Building it, MA goes inside that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking in natural set phrases is speaking the way native users of a language do.

clue.text: 8 dead on radio broadcast before 50

indicators.note: before puts the rearranged letters ahead of the numeral
broadcast means scattered, so these letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: News of a death is announced over the airwaves before the age of fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is IDIOMATICALLY: the simile is 'as dead as a ___'.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock simile 'dead as a doornail' means utterly lifeless, and the two lights complete it.

clue.text: Avoid this by not staying up too long, or else dad's furious

definitions.text: Avoid this by not staying up too long

indicators.note: furious suggests wild agitation, so these letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A parent warns a child not to stay up late, or else Dad will be livid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staying up' sounds like bedtime, but it means staying on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Riders who stay mounted for hours get chafed buttocks, so riding briefly prevents that soreness.

clue.text: Crazy rockstar retires to nurse a cold

indicators.note: retires says the hidden letters are read backwards
to nurse is to hold close, so the two words hold the letters within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wild rock musician steps back from touring to recover from a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'nurse a cold' as the definition, but the answer means only a cold: 'to nurse' says the words hold the letters, and 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Coryza is the medical term for inflammation of the nose's mucous membrane, the common cold.

clue.text: Spin-off comes along, making monsters

indicators.note: off says the letters for spin are taken away

parts.note: comes along means makes headway, progresses
PR, public relations, is spin

explanation.surface: A spin-off show turns up and creates new monsters for its franchise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin-off' looks like a single noun, but it splits into spin (PR) and the instruction off.
explanation.definitionFit: Female ogres are fairy-tale monsters, giants that eat people.

clue.text: Red Indian, half American

parts.note: florid means ruddy, red in the face

indicators.note: half takes the back three of the six letters of the word Indian

explanation.surface: A description of a Native American of mixed heritage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red Indian' looks like one phrase but must be split into two pieces; 'half' takes the back three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Florida is an American, so a resident of that state fits.

clue.text: Lodger wanted to get radical round sleazy motel

indicators.note: round says the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: a radical is a root, in maths and in language

indicators.note: sleazy suggests something disreputable and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newly radical landlord takes on a seedy roadside motel and seeks a tenant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lodger wanted' is the wording of a notice in a window, not a description of a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign offering accommodation for rent is posted when a landlord wants a paying tenant.

clue.text: Bill's partner by the end of August is 8 bald

parts.note: lovers bill and coo, so coo is the partner of bill

indicators.note: the end of picks the final letter of the month's name

explanation.surface: A man's companion, by late August, has lost all his hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name (Bill and Ben), but it is the verb in 'bill and coo'. 8 is IDIOMATICALLY: the simile is 'as bald as a ___'.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock simile 'bald as a coot' comes from the white patch on the waterbird's head.

clue.text: See 20
Attack and capture

definitions.meaning: an attack here is a sudden fit, as in an epileptic fit
capture means the taking hold of something, as with goods confiscated

explanation.surface: A military order to assault and take a position.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a medical fit and the act of taking possession, as in a customs haul.

clue.text: Is minister's back covered by trip to the bank?

indicators.note: covered by says the following word wraps around what comes before

parts.note: a ride is a trip or journey

indicators.note: back says the letters are turned to read the other way

parts.note: taken as written
Rev is short for Reverend, the title of a minister

explanation.surface: A curious question about whether a clergyman's return is paid for by a trip to the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' suggests money but means the edge of a river, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Land along the edge of a river is its bank, so the question mark marks a sense other than finance.

clue.text: In context, remedy is harsh

indicators.note: In says the letters sit within the next words, spanning the comma

explanation.surface: A medical cure, seen in its full setting, proves severe.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme measures are severe or drastic ones, so harsh is a near-synonym.

clue.text: Tramp welcomes compiler portfolio

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the first piece takes the other inside

parts.note: a dosser is British slang for a tramp or rough sleeper
the compiler of the crossword refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: A homeless person greets a crossword setter carrying a folder of papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A dossier is a collection of documents on one subject, much like a portfolio of papers.

clue.text: 8 pure ambition by Poles at the moment

parts.note: drive is energy and ambition
N is the north pole
S is the south pole
at the moment means now

explanation.surface: A spotless reputation, ambition and Polish connections are all in play right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests people from Poland but gives the two compass poles, N and S. 8 is IDIOMATICALLY: the simile is 'as pure as the ___'.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock simile 'pure as the driven snow' means wholly innocent, and the two lights complete it.

clue.text: State queen falls in station

definitions.meaning: an Australian state whose capital is Melbourne
the British monarch who reigned from 1837 to 1901
the great waterfall on the Zambezi

explanation.surface: A monarch takes a tumble in a railway terminus.
explanation.walkthrough: Four definitions in a row; London's Victoria is a main rail station.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to an Australian state, a long-reigning queen, African falls and a London terminus.

clue.text: Asian, drunk, reported by office worker

indicators.note: reported means passed on in speech, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: a Thai is an Asian, and pissed is British slang for drunk

explanation.surface: An inebriated Asian person is reported to the authorities by a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pissed' means drunk in British English, not angry as in American use.
explanation.definitionFit: A typist is a clerical employee who types documents, an office job.

clue.text: 8 pleased with drink

definitions.meaning: with 8 read as idiomatically, 'as pleased as ___' names the puppet show's gleeful hero
a mixed drink of spirits, fruit and spice served from a bowl

explanation.surface: Someone happy to be offered a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Punch is the hook-nosed puppet of British Punch and Judy shows, famously self-satisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: The simile 'pleased as Punch' means delighted, and the same word is a party drink.

clue.text: South of France about to welcome learners and immerse them in French life — how tedious!

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the learners go inside
about says the word is turned to read the other way

parts.note: sud is French for south
L is a learner driver's plate, so two learners are LL

indicators.note: immerse means plunge into, so the learners are put inside the next word

parts.note: vie is French for life
them refers back to the learners

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker takes learners to the south of France to steep them in French life, and finds it dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the French word for south back to front; L is the learner-driver plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Dullsville is informal for a boring place or situation, the exclamation of someone bored.

clue.text: See 9
Heartless, extravagant and still living

indicators.note: heartless says the middle of the word is removed, leaving its two ends

explanation.surface: Someone cruel and spendthrift, yet still alive and kicking.
explanation.definitionFit: Extant means still in existence, surviving, as with a species not yet extinct.

clue.text: Essentially dizzy and hyperactive with wind

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence, the very centre of the word
active suggests lively movement, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A dizzy, overexcited child with a touch of indigestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hyperactive' must split in two, its second half signalling a rearrangement of its first.
explanation.definitionFit: A zephyr is a soft gentle breeze, named after the Greek god of the west wind.
